Definition: from the base of G977; food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law:--meat, victuals.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses brōma for food, meat. Across its 15 occurrences the word stays true to that sense, whether it stands in 1 Corinthians or in 1 Timothy. That steadiness is what makes it worth knowing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that brōma proves nothing in Scripture is filler. Food, meat turns up again and again because God wants it noticed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
